summary: Phase 2 (multi-tenant + self-service governance) backend testing complete. Created /app/backend/tests/test_governance_phase2.py with 26 tests covering event_id propagation across the FREK-Chain (identity emit, stage transition, revocation, walkin_emit, access_scan), spec_version=1.0.0 versioning, list/filter endpoints, /chain/events aggregation, /chain/status events list, backwards-compat verify on legacy blocks, and full self-service /admin/clients lifecycle (create/rotate/patch/soft-delete + 401 'Client desactive' enforcement). Result: 26/26 PASSED. Ran regression on Phase 1 (test_governance_phase1.py: all pass) and full v1 suite (79/81 pass; 2 pre-existing legacy test failures in test_frek_v1_api.py are NOT Phase 2 regressions).

minor.issue: Spec says missing X-Admin-Key should return 403, but FastAPI returns 422 because Header(...) is declared as required. Wrong key correctly returns 403. Either change to Header(None) + manual 403, or update spec to accept 422 for missing header. Test accepts both.

Token revocation on rotate writes revoked=true to db.frek_tokens, but get_current_client in auth.py does NOT check the frek_tokens collection — it only validates JWT signature and client.active flag. So tokens issued before rotate remain technically valid until JWT expiry (24h). The behaviour is acceptable for active=false flow (caught via client.active check), but the rotate flow does not actually invalidate in-flight bearer tokens. Test_existing_token_rejected_after_deactivation passes only because deactivation sets active=false. A pure rotate (without deactivation) would NOT invalidate existing tokens. Recommend either: (a) add revoked check in get_current_client by hashing the bearer token and looking up frek_tokens, or (b) clarify spec that rotate only affects future /auth/token calls.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Decide whether to enforce 403 (vs 422) for missing X-Admin-Key — if yes, switch to Header(None) and explicit None check in verify_admin_key.

OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED: Make /clients/{id}/rotate truly invalidate in-flight tokens by adding a token-revocation lookup in get_current_client (compare hash_secret(bearer_token) against frek_tokens.revoked).
Cleanup: Phase 2 introduced TEST_phase2_* clients and identities in DB during testing; consider a periodic prune script for TEST_-prefixed data.
critical_code_review_comments: chain.py append_block: clean implementation, event_id is sparse-indexed and properly included in compute_block_hash. Backwards-compat fallback in verify_chain (legacy hash recomputation when event_id/spec_version are absent) works as intended — verified on 99 legacy blocks + new blocks (verify returns valid=true).
service.py notarize_event passes event_id correctly. All 3 staff scan endpoints (access_scan, jeton_tx, walkin_emit) propagate badge.event/request.event consistently.
admin.py is well structured: rotate, patch, soft-delete all idempotent on 404, soft-delete preserves audit trail, active_only filter works.
auth.py get_current_client: properly rejects inactive clients (401 'Client desactive') but does NOT check token revocation flag in db.frek_tokens. See minor issue above.
FastAPI Header(...) being required produces 422 not 403 — consistent FastAPI behaviour but inconsistent with stated 403 spec.
models.py: ClientInfoResponse correctly exposes active/event/last_used_at/rotated_at; secret_hash never leaks (excluded in list query projection).
/notary/chain/events aggregation uses MongoDB pipeline cleanly; sorts by last_block_at desc; payload_types deduplicated.
